Weighted Frequency Table for a Discrete Variable (SCF Multiply-Imputed Data)

Source: R/scf_freq.R
scf_freq.Rd

Computes a weighted frequency table for a discrete variable using multiply-imputed SCF data. Applies svytotal() (or svyby() for grouped tables) to each implicate, combines estimates using Rubin's Rules, and returns a clean table of categories, weighted counts, and percentages.

scf_freq(design, var, by = NULL, max_cats = 20)

Arguments

design

A multiply-imputed svrepdesign object, typically created by scf_load().

var

A one-sided formula specifying the discrete variable to tabulate, e.g., ~edcl.

by

Optional one-sided formula indicating a grouping variable, e.g., ~race.

max_cats

Integer. Maximum number of unique categories allowed (default is 20).

Value

A data.frame with the following columns:

  • category: Levels of the focal variable (or var:by combinations if grouped)

  • group: Value of the by variable if specified (otherwise NA)

  • estimated_count: Weighted population counts

  • percent: Weighted percentage (within group if by is specified)

  • cum_percent: Cumulative percentage (within group if by is specified)

The returned object also includes an "implicates" attribute containing individual implicate-level estimates for further inspection or diagnostics.

Details

This function handles multiply-imputed SCF data using Rubin's Rules and is ideal for summarizing variables like race, education, marital status, or any discrete group.

For grouped tables (by specified), percentages are computed within each group.

See also

svytotal(), svyby(), scf_MIcombine(), scf_plot_dbar()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
scf_freq(scf2022, ~race)
scf_freq(scf2022, ~married, by = ~race)
} # }
